title: Crop: An Analytical Cost Model for Cross-Platform Performance Prediction of Tensor Programs
problem: Learn-based cost models for tensor compiler auto-tuning suffer from poor cross-platform generalization, requiring expensive per-platform performance data collection during deployment.
motivation: Eliminating platform-specific data collection overhead is essential for practical deployment of tensor compilers across diverse hardware platforms.
method: Proposes Crop, an analytical cost model that predicts tensor program performance across platforms without platform-specific training data. Uses mathematical modeling to capture hardware-agnostic and hardware-specific performance factors.
key_novelty: An analytical cost model approach for cross-platform tensor performance prediction that eliminates the need for platform-specific training data, unlike learn-based models.
contributions: Analytical cost model for cross-platform tensor program performance prediction
Eliminates per-platform performance data collection overhead during deployment
Demonstrates improved generalization across hardware platforms compared to learn-based approaches

metrics.accuracy: prediction accuracy relative to actual execution time

primary_theme: analytical cost models for cross-platform tensor compilation
